recreation_brief: 1. Set the slide background to solid white (#FFFFFF), no gradient or texture. 2. Draw the outer border frame: a no-fill rectangle along all four slide edges (inset about 1% from each edge), thin outline #B22222 (~1pt). 3. Place the title: a text box centered horizontally at y 10-20% of slide height, containing 'Choice of K - Neighborhood Size' in bold red #CC0000, sans-serif, ~32pt, center-aligned. 4. Place the slide-number badge: a circle centered at ~x 91%, y 10% of the slide, fill #FFFF99, thin dark outline #333333, containing the text '56' centered in dark #333333 (~14pt). 5. Draw the content box: a rounded-corner rectangle spanning x 5-95%, y 25-95% of the slide, white #FFFFFF fill, thin red #B22222 outline (~1.5pt). 6. Inside the content box, add a left-aligned text box starting at x ~8% of slide width holding a two-level list: main level = round bullet markers, red bold #CC0000, ~22pt; sub-level = dash '-' markers, indented, dark #333333, ~18pt. 7. Main bullet 1 'Small K' with two sub-bullets: 'Creates many small regions for each class'; and 'May lead to non-smooth decision boundaries and over-fit' with the phrase 'and over-fit' in red bold #CC0000 (rest of the line dark #333333). 8. Main bullet 2 'Large K' with two sub-bullets: 'Creates fewer larger regions'; and 'Usually leads to smoother decision boundaries (caution: too smooth decision boundary can under-fit). High bias to classes with larger members' with 'under-fit' and 'High bias' in red bold #CC0000. 9. Main bullet 3 'Choosing K' with three sub-bullets: 'Often data dependent and heuristic based'; 'Or using cross-validation (using some held-out data)'; and 'In general, a K too small or too big is bad!' with the entire line in red bold #CC0000. 10. Add one final main-level bullet (round red marker) with no text at the bottom of the list, reproducing the captured mid-build state. 11. Do NOT draw the small gray (#999999) plus/cross mark near the top-center of the content box - it is a mouse-cursor recording artifact, not slide content.
